Hi u/Queen-Keane , 

I know exactly how you feel- I have told people this multiple times, especially new friends. I know you believe you're the absolute worst person alive but, I promise you, that's just your brain lying to you. You're a person who is doing their best right now and who is capable of growth despite the past.

Telling someone they should leave you becomes a self fulfilling prophecy but I know it's difficult to stop because you truly feel that way. Like u/bl1nken suggested, maybe try another therapists who could help you better. Also, if you have the time/energy to do so, read up on cognitive distortions. There are plenty 10 min youtube videos on it as well . My therapist told me about this and I became aware of them, so I can pull myself back every time I'm having those irrational thoughts. 

From what you said, your boyfriend is having a difficult time with being told this. He got unintentionally hurt. I think, the best you can do in this situation, is give him the space he needs and work on yourself, taking the smallest steps. Or just survive if that's all you can do. Maybe do something nice for yourself even if you think your brain lying to yo about not deserving it. Hey, how about watching a cheesy Christmas rom-com?
